parsed.rationale: The cluster row carries an empty `members` array and all structural evidence fields (`differing_slots`, `jaccard`, `shared_field_count`, `shared_ancestor`) are null, meaning no concrete field-level or shape-level evidence was surfaced to ground any refactor recommendation. The cluster_id does name two plausible participants — `MockStructuredAnalytics.CPUSessionEventProxy__Playback` in `AnalyticsTesting` (a mock/test support file by naming convention) and `CPUSessionEvent` in `PlaybackCore/Analytics/PlaybackAnalytics.swift` — but without member lists or Jaccard similarity scores it is impossible to verify whether the subset relationship is real or artefactual. Recommending an extraction or protocol change without that evidence would risk collapsing a deliberate mock-vs-production boundary. Per the decision rules, when evidence cannot be grounded in the cluster row, `no-action` with reason_class `coincidental` is the correct conservative choice.
